loss_objective: Collector sending queue uses the persistent file_storage extension (host-mounted, survives container recreation). Queued telemetry that has been accepted into the queue therefore persists across a collector restart and is flushed on recovery (verified: 40 pre-restart queued traces delivered after restart). During a transient backend outage caused by an egress block that yields timeouts, the opensearch exporter treats the failure as retryable and buffers items in the persistent queue until the backend returns (no loss; drained in 40.6s). A hard/permanent backend rejection (e.g. connection refused) is classified as non-retryable by the opensearch exporter and is dropped immediately (acknowledged loss on permanent failure).
queue_bounded: sending_queue.queue_size=5000 batches (explicit bound); file_storage directory host-mounted at /opt/mct-security-stack/data/otel-file-storage; on-disk footprint bounded by queue_size x batch size; create_directory:true
retry_bounded: retry_on_failure: enabled=true, initial_interval=5s, max_interval=30s, max_elapsed_time=300s (capped 5-minute retry window before permanent drop)

evidence.loss_objective: Verified by restart test (see restart_tested): 40 traces enqueued while egress blocked, collector restarted, after unblock the pre-restart queued traces were exported (e.g. trace 35b9c78899acc80aa4cd7976812e5252 -> doc xD0CVKABomKEMWVwrwAr). Persistent queue survived the restart.
evidence.queue_bounded: sending_queue.queue_size=5000 (live metric otelcol_exporter_queue_capacity=5000). file_storage host-mounted -> bounded on disk by queue_size x batch size.
evidence.retry_bounded: retry_on_failure max_elapsed_time=300s caps retries; beyond that the item is dropped (bounded retry).
evidence.drop_metric: otelcol_exporter_send_failed_spans exposed on prometheus :8889 (verified present, value 0 at time of capture; increments on permanent drop). Also otelcol_exporter_queue_capacity and otelcol_exporter_queue_size exposed.
evidence.outage_peak_depth: Source-specific egress block via host DOCKER-USER: 'iptables -I DOCKER-USER -s 172.20.0.18 -d 172.20.0.3 -p tcp --dport 9200 -j DROP' (collector src -> opensearch dst only; OpenSearch itself kept running and serving other clients). 80 OTLP traces injected during a 71s outage; peak persistent-queue depth observed = 16 trace batches (otelcol_exporter_queue_size{data_type=traces}=16).
evidence.drain_time: After removing the DOCKER-USER rule, the collector flushed the queued backlog; queue reached 0 (otelcol_exporter_queue_size=0) 40.6s after unblock. One injected trace (7b7c80094df7b6a9cbab5292b206c0e7) confirmed present in ss4o_traces-otel-mct-soc (doc Wz0CVKABomKEMWVwEwCq).
evidence.restart_tested: 40 traces queued while egress blocked; 'docker restart mct-otel-collector' completed in 12.5s, health 127.0.0.1:13133 -> 200; persistent queue + file_storage bind mount preserved queued data; after unblock the pre-restart queued traces were exported. No telemetry loss across restart.
evidence.classa_independent: During the collector backend outage, a Class-A Wazuh->IRIS webhook canary POST to http://shuffle-backend:5001/api/v1/hooks/webhook_e3fec000-555f-4e81-9497-77b7c91c5b98 returned HTTP 200 (trigger accepted). The Shuffle->IRIS data path is architecturally independent of the telemetry collector egress; telemetry failure did not block Class-A delivery.

evidence.cardinality_before: Before the queue change the cardinality budget was enforced by: (1) attributes/allowlist processor deleting high-cardinality/sensitive keys (client/source/host/net .ip/.address/.port, and password|secret|token|api_key|authorization|credential patterns); (2) memory_limiter limit_mib=256 spike_limit_mib=64; (3) explicit sending_queue.queue_size=5000. All present in collector.yaml at baseline.
evidence.cardinality_after: After the persistent-queue change the attributes/allowlist processor, memory_limiter, and explicit queue_size bound remain unchanged and still enforce the cardinality budget (queue change is additive; no cardinality control removed). Both before/after states = controls present (true).
evidence.sensitive_scan_clean: Recent trace doc in ss4o_traces-otel-mct-soc (e.g. _id mDxGUaABomKEMWVwcv8Y) stores attributes = alert_id, data_stream, delivery_state, event_type, reconciliation_state, rule_id, source and resource service.name/service.environment only. No client.address / source.ip / host.ip / net.peer.ip / token / secret / authorization / credential keys present. Sensitive attributes are dropped by the attributes/allowlist processor before export.
